cast.name: Victor
cast.canonical: a lean, slightly hunched young man with untidy dark hair, round glasses, dark shadowed feverish eyes, wearing a stained lab apron
cast.anchor: round glasses, a stained lab apron and dark shadowed eyes

cast.name: the Creature
cast.canonical: a very tall gaunt figure, chalk-white skin, bald head with one bold black stitch-seam across the brow, a bolt at the neck, heavy seams on the arms, deep sorrowful hollow eyes, sharp teeth, ragged shirt
cast.anchor: tallest gaunt bald body, a brow stitch-seam, a neck bolt and sorrowful hollow eyes

cast.name: Clerval
cast.canonical: a cheerful upright young man in a black top hat and a long travel scarf, a book of poems under his arm, bright smiling face
cast.anchor: a black top hat, a long scarf and a book under the arm

cast.name: Elizabeth
cast.canonical: a gentle graceful young woman with bright fair golden hair in a long braid under a white bonnet, an oval locket at her throat and a shoulder shawl
cast.anchor: bright fair golden hair, a white bonnet, an oval locket and a shawl

panels.scene: a cluttered attic laboratory at 1am, rain on the window, a guttering candle, the young scientist bent over a large covered body on a slab, instruments everywhere
panels.composition: wide establishing; Victor small in the big dim room

teen.narration: TWO YEARS OF SECRET LABOUR COME DOWN TO THIS ONE RAINY NIGHT.

bubbles.speaker: victor
bubbles.text: TONIGHT... IT LIVES.
It was on a dreary night of November that I beheld the accomplishment of my toils.

panels.scene: the newborn creature lying on a slab in the lower half of the frame, one dull yellow eye just opening, a candle beside it; the whole upper area is dark empty attic air
panels.composition: medium; creature low in frame, empty top band

bubbles.text: I saw the dull yellow eye of the creature open; it breathed hard, and a convulsive motion agitated its limbs.

panels.scene: the scientist steps back staring, the tall new-made creature half-rising, its proportions grand but wrong
panels.composition: two-shot at a distance; creature dim behind

teen.narration: HE HAD CHOSEN EVERY PART TO BE BEAUTIFUL. HE WAS WRONG.

bubbles.text: His limbs were in proportion, and I had selected his features as beautiful. Beautiful! Great God!

panels.scene: the tall creature standing in the lower portion, its yellow stitched face and long black hair lit by candlelight, Victor recoiling to one side; open dark empty space above the figures
panels.composition: wide; figures low, empty top band

teen.narration: THE DETAILS THAT SHOULD HAVE BEEN LOVELY MADE IT ONLY MORE HORRIBLE.

bubbles.text: His yellow skin scarcely covered the work of muscles and arteries beneath; his hair was of a lustrous black, and flowing; his teeth of a pearly whiteness

panels.scene: Victor standing small in the lower half of the frame, clutching his chest in disgust and dread, an empty dim room stretching above him
panels.composition: medium; Victor low, empty top band

teen.narration: IN ONE INSTANT, HIS LIFELONG DREAM CURDLED INTO NIGHTMARE.

bubbles.speaker: victor
bubbles.text: WHAT HAVE I MADE?
now that I had finished, the beauty of the dream vanished, and breathless horror and disgust filled my heart.

panels.scene: the scientist bursting out of the laboratory door and pacing his bedchamber in his clothes, unable to sleep

teen.narration: HE COULD NOT BEAR TO LOOK AT IT. SO HE RAN — AND TRIED TO SLEEP.

bubbles.text: Unable to endure the aspect of the being I had created, I rushed out of the room

panels.scene: a feverish dream: a lovely young woman in a street, embraced, then turning grey and corpse-like, grave-worms in a shroud, surreal and grim
panels.composition: medium dream-vision; Elizabeth turning to a corpse

teen.narration: BUT SLEEP BROUGHT WORSE: HE KISSED HIS BELOVED ELIZABETH, AND SHE ROTTED INTO A CORPSE IN HIS ARMS.

bubbles.text: I thought I saw Elizabeth, in the bloom of health, walking in the streets of Ingolstadt.

panels.scene: the scientist waking in cold sweat by moonlight to find the towering creature beside his bed, lifting the bed-curtain, staring down at him
panels.composition: wide; creature looming over the bed, Victor small

teen.narration: HE WOKE... AND IT WAS STANDING OVER HIM.

bubbles.text: I beheld the wretch … the miserable monster whom I had created.

panels.scene: the creature at medium distance standing in the lower half, jaws parted muttering wordless sounds, a strange grin, one hand reaching; empty misty space above
panels.composition: medium; creature low, empty top band

teen.narration: IT TRIED TO SPEAK — MAYBE EVEN TO SMILE. VICTOR SAW ONLY A MONSTER.

bubbles.text: His jaws opened, and he muttered some inarticulate sounds, while a grin wrinkled his cheeks.

panels.scene: the creature's hand stretched out to detain him as the scientist tears free and bolts down a staircase
panels.composition: medium; Victor fleeing foreground, hand reaching behind

teen.narration: THE OUTSTRETCHED HAND MIGHT HAVE MEANT STAY. HE READ IT AS A THREAT.

bubbles.text: one hand was stretched out, seemingly to detain me, but I escaped and rushed downstairs.

panels.scene: the scientist pacing a rainy courtyard all night, terrified, listening for footsteps
panels.composition: medium; Victor alone in the yard

teen.narration: HE HID IN THE COURTYARD TILL DAWN, FLINCHING AT EVERY SOUND.

bubbles.text: No mortal could support the horror of that countenance.

panels.scene: grey wet dawn over the town, a white church steeple and clock showing six, the exhausted scientist in the empty street

teen.narration: MORNING CAME, DISMAL AND WET. HE DARED NOT GO HOME.

bubbles.text: Morning, dismal and wet, at length dawned

panels.scene: the scientist hurrying through the streets in the rain, not daring to look behind him, dread on his face

teen.narration: HE WALKED AND WALKED, TRYING TO OUTRUN HIS OWN FEAR.

bubbles.text: My heart palpitated in the sickness of fear, and I hurried on with irregular steps, not daring to look about me

panels.scene: a Swiss coach stops in the street and a cheerful young friend springs out, arms wide, delighted to see the pale scientist
panels.composition: wide; coach and Clerval, Victor gaunt

teen.narration: THEN, LIKE A RESCUE, HIS DEAREST FRIEND CLERVAL STEPPED OFF THE COACH.

bubbles.speaker: clerval
bubbles.text: MY DEAR FRANKENSTEIN, HOW GLAD I AM TO SEE YOU!
I grasped his hand, and in a moment forgot my horror and misfortune

panels.scene: the two friends walking toward the college, the scientist secretly dreading what waits in his rooms

teen.narration: BUT ONE TERROR GNAWED AT HIM: WAS THE CREATURE STILL UP THERE?

bubbles.text: I dreaded to behold this monster, but I feared still more that Henry should see him.

panels.scene: the scientist flinging his apartment door wide with dread, bracing for a specter — but the room is empty
panels.composition: medium; Victor at the thrown-open door, empty room

teen.narration: HE THREW THE DOOR OPEN LIKE A CHILD DARING A GHOST... AND FOUND NOTHING. IT HAD FLED.

bubbles.text: I threw the door forcibly open, as children are accustomed to do when they expect a spectre to stand in waiting for them on the other side; but nothing appeared.

panels.scene: at breakfast the scientist laughs wildly and leaps over chairs, then collapses in a fit, his friend horrified

teen.narration: RELIEF TIPPED INTO MADNESS. HE LAUGHED, RAVED, AND FELL.

bubbles.speaker: victor
bubbles.text: SAVE ME! SAVE ME!
I imagined that the monster seized me; I struggled furiously and fell down in a fit.

panels.scene: a sickroom over the seasons, the friend faithfully nursing the scientist, spring buds finally at the window
panels.composition: wide; Clerval tending Victor, spring window

teen.narration: A NERVOUS FEVER TOOK HIM FOR MONTHS. HENRY NURSED HIM BACK — NEVER GUESSING THE REAL CAUSE. THE MAKER SURVIVED. HIS SECRET DID NOT DIE.

bubbles.text: This was the commencement of a nervous fever which confined me for several months. During all that time Henry was my only nurse.
